Are you a law student passionate about criminal justice? 

Apply to the Cato University Criminal Justice Symposium — a rigorous three-day program at Cato's DC headquarters, August 6–8. 

Hear from legal fellow @foxmike90 as he previews some discussion topics of Cato’s Criminal Justice Symposium.
 
Learn more: ow.ly/pjTp50YTEoP  
Apply here: ow.ly/C9Ex50YTEoN

Washington’s Anthropic whiplash teaches us that with emergent technologies, picking winners and losers can backfire—especially in AI, where markets are in constant flux. Light-touch rules may beat heavy-handed regulations, argues Cato’s Juan Londoño.
ow.ly/U8iu50YTCEA

Social Security is widely described as self-financed. It isn't. Since 2010, the Treasury has borrowed more than $1.5 trillion to pay benefits — and the trust fund runs dry in 2032.  
 
Join us for an expert event, discussing reform strategies that address the program’s structural flaws and prevent Social Security from worsening the debt crisis. Featuring @RominaBoccia of the Cato Institute, @JessicaBRiedl of the Brookings Institution, and @EugeneSteuerle of the Urban Institute. 
 
Register: ow.l

There are significant policy questions raised by the situation between Anthropic and the Pentagon. “These policy questions, however, should be appropriately decided not by bureaucrats or the courts, but by Congress,” argues Cato’s @jrhuddles. 
  
ow.ly/WNb950YTgTO

In 2021, over 135 countries agreed to end unilateral digital services taxes. Now, the DSTs have reemerged as part of the transatlantic debate over how to tax the digital economy. 
  
Join us for a conversation with leading European voices on the future of digital taxation, featuring Cato’s @adamnmichel, @ahellmanndc of the Tholos Foundation, @crisberechet of Tax Foundation Europe, and @MatBauerEcon of the European Centre for International Political Economy. 

Register: ow.ly/CUGA50YTEtr

Surgical AI is advancing fast—but who should “govern” it? Not the FDA. Not surgeons. Centralized gatekeeping risks slowing innovation, protecting insiders, and blurring accountability. Start with patient autonomy and clear liability instead, says @dr4liberty.

ow.ly/7soO50YTkYR

Extending current tax and spending policies could add $4.2 trillion to deficits over the next decade—rising to $5.5 trillion if temporary provisions become permanent. Fiscal responsibility demands honest accounting, says Cato’s @jeffreyamiron.

Learn more: ow.ly/E9Mi50YTkUp

While deeply flawed and perhaps rushed, there was nevertheless a debate on Capitol Hill about US military action in Afghanistan and the invasion of Iraq. For the Iran war, there was nothing comparable, writes Cato's @brandan_buck. 

ow.ly/gGXO50YTEla
The case for limited government, in one sentence, from P. J. O’Rourke.

"The school system didn't allow me to be everything that I am," says Tasha Ellis, a 20-year teaching veteran. So, she built her own microschool. 

At Legacy Learning Loft, learning is personal — and the results speak for themselves. Learn more from @ColleenHroncich. 

ow.ly/Q1KB50YR7Wg

The GUARD Act would ban minors from AI tools, strip parents of choices, and force all users into risky age-verification schemes. It's likely unconstitutional—and bad policy that leaves kids and families less prepared, not safer, say Cato’s Jennifer Huddleston and Juan Londoño.

Learn more: ow.ly/SbUu50YTcQn

Please join us for a cocktail reception and conversation in NYC on May 5.

Featuring:
🔹 @johanknorberg, Senior Fellow
🔹 @David_J_Bier, Director of Immigration Studies and the Selz Foundation Chair in Immigration Policy
🔹 @ConLawWarrior, Senior Vice President for Legal Studies
🔹 Harrison Moar, Senior Vice President for Marketing and Partnerships
🔹 Peter Goettler, President and CEO
 
Register here: ow.ly/ezkH50YTEa9.
The Trump administration's dubious logic that the Iran ceasefire "pauses" the 60-day clock is the latest proof the War Powers Resolution no longer works, explains Cato scholar @katherinet57.

The Bank Secrecy Act forces banks to file 75,000 reports a day at an annual cost of $59 billion—yet it triggered only 370 IRS investigations last year. Congress should repeal this failed surveillance regime and respect Americans' financial privacy, argues Cato’s @EconWithNick.
ow.ly/XHA650YTbuk

The Supreme Court just made it harder to use race when drawing voting districts. But here’s the catch—partisan gerrymandering is still allowed, and since race and politics often overlap, the result could still sort voters by race in less obvious ways. 
Read more: ow.ly/c2ES50YSYem

As America approaches the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, "Proclaiming Liberty” by @TimothySandefur revisits the revolutionary summer of 1776 through the minds of John Adams and Thomas Jefferson.
nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1XxygmyDQ…

The best way to make housing affordable? Allow more building.

That means removing government-imposed barriers and cost pressures on new construction, Cato’s @sslivinski explains.

Learn more in the “Cato Handbook on Affordability”: ow.ly/zH4N50YSQl5
